text.p: The following are some of the front page stories in the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers. Reuters has not checked these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- WHY GLOBO HAS BECOME MORE TRANSPARENT

Roberto Marinho, the president and major shareholder of the Globo media empire, and his three sons have never liked giving interviews. But they have changed under pressure from the market because they realize their far-reaching organization needs to be more transparent.
-- UNITED STATES AND CANADA PRESSURE FOR ALCA ACCORD

The United States and Canada are pressuring the Mercosur countries to reach an agreement for an American Free Trade region (Alca) by the 2003. The Mercosur partners, led by Brazil, want to delay an agreement until 2005.
-- CVRD VAL SA TENDER DOCUMENT TO BE READY NEXT WEEK
Planning Minister Antonio Kandir said the final tender documents for the privatization of mining giant Vale do Rio Doce will be ready by next week.
-- CENTRAL BANK STARTS INTERNAL BOND FRAUD PROBE
Brazil's central bank has opened up an internal probe to investigate how it allowed a widespread state and municipal bond scheme to flourish.
-- LOWER HOUSE TO VOTE ON RE-ELECTION
The Lower House of Congress is expected to approve a constitutional amendment allowing incumbent presidents to run for a second term in office in a second round vote today.
-- CONGRESSMEN PROPOSE AMNESTY FOR BLACK MARKET FOREX TRADERS

A congressional committee probing a widespread state and municipal bond scam, have proposed an amnesty for black market forex dealers in exchange for information on the public officials who designed the fraud.
